Author: M.Laxman
Bench: M.Laxman
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice M.Laxman
 Criminal Petition No.8522 of 2018
Order:

1. The Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., by the petitioner/accused No.4 to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.696 of 2016, on the file of the Court of the learned XVII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 120-B and 506 of IPC.

entities.text: XVII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The sum and substance of the case of the prosecution is that accused Nos.1 to 3 are the absolute owners of house property bearing No.1-1-385, Gandhi Nagar, Bakaram, Hyderabad.
Respondent No.2 herein/complainant is the tenant of accused Nos.1 to 3.
While so, the petitioner herein, who is a developer, agreed to develop the land having entered into development agreement with the original owners.
Accused Nos.1 to 3 agreed to pay a sum of Rs.15,40,000/- to respondent No.2 towards goodwill gesture.

Respondent No.2, having interested to buy a flat in the proposed building,
approached the petitioner herein.

Upon which, the petitioner agreed to sell flat No.303,
admeasuring 1600 sft., for a total sale consideration of Rs.68,40,000/-.

Out of the said amount,
Rs.15,40,000/-was agreed to be treated as advance and subsequently, Rs.10,00,000/- was paid by the petitioner.
After such agreement, there was extension of the constructed area on account of fresh development agreement entered by the petitioner with neighbouring land owner.
Resultantly, the original flats were changed.
Thereby, originally agreed area of flat No.303, which was road side, was reduced to 1060 sq.ft., from 1600 sq.fts.
Due to such change, respondent No.2 was asked to purchase flat No.301 on the same floor, which was to an extent of 1600 sq.fts, but he did not show any interest as it was not on the road side.
When respondent No.2 requested to pay back his amount, the petitioner refused to do so.
Hence, the present complaint.

3. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the complainant has filed a civil suit for recovery of the amounts due under the agreement and he never sought a specific performance.
To give a colour of civil dispute into criminal, the present criminal case has been foisted against the petitioner.
According to him, there is no intention on the part of the petitioner not to comply with the agreement.

As there was extension of area of originally agreed flat No.303,
the petitioner asked the complainant to purchase another flat, which was on the same floor but he did not agree for the same, since the said flat was not on the road side.
It is also his contention that the complainant has not paid the balance amount in installments.
In the said circumstances, a legal notice dated 24.11.2014 intimating the cancellation of agreement of sale.

Thereafter, a reply notice was issued by the complainant, whereunder he has clearly claimed that the flat initially agreed to Siddineni Ramakrishna vs The State Of Telangana on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45009394/

sentences.text: sell was on the road side, but the flat later agreed to allot was not on the road side.
Hence, he did not evince any interest.
4. The learned Assistant Public Prosecutor opposed to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.696 of 2016.
5. There is no dispute that there is an agreement of sale between both the parties.

In the agreement,
Rs.15,40,000/- was agreed to give as discount in the sale price of the flat going to be purchased by the complainant, in lieu of undertaking given by the complainant to vacate the premises voluntarily without creating any disturbance for the development of the project.
The cost of the flat was Rs.68,40,000/- and Rs.15,40,000/- which agreed to discount, was treated as an advance amount and the balance amount was 53,00,000/-.
Out of that amount, Rs.10,00,000/- was paid at the time of agreement and the balance amount to be paid was Rs.43,00,000/- and the same was agreed to pay on installments as per the agreement.
Absolutely, there is no material on record to show that the complainant tried to comply with the said condition.
In fact, there is a change of flat on account of extension of the area of development on account of entering into development agreement with neighbouring land owner.
The complainant allegedly offered to purchase similar area of flat in the same floor but he has not shown any interest as the previous flat was on the road side.
There is no refusal on the part of the petitioner to comply the conditions and in fact, a notice was issued for terminating the agreement and agreed to refund the amount, which is not accepted.
Subsequent to the said notice, present complainant has been filed.
6. It appears from the facts of the case that the dispute is purely civil in nature and this complaint is filed to settle the civil dispute between the parties.
Civil litigation has been given colour of criminality.
7. Accordingly, this criminal petition is allowed.
The proceedings in C.C.No.696 of 2016, on the file of the Court of the learned XVII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad, are hereby quashed.
